claims.text: The feedstock is FeCoNiCrAl high-entropy alloy powder in the 15–45 μm size range.
Standard HVAF-i7 settings with 15–45 μm feedstock produce coatings of acceptable quality but inadequate thickness.
The proposed intervention is to reduce the HVAF-i7 nozzle-to-substrate distance to approximately 300–350 mm.
Reducing the HVAF-i7 spray distance to 300–350 mm increases particle velocity.
The reduced spray distance increases particle kinetic energy.
Higher particle velocity enhances momentum transfer during impact.
Improved impact-energy transfer promotes particle flattening.
Improved impact-energy transfer promotes inter-splat bonding.
Improved particle flattening and inter-splat bonding increase deposition efficiency.
The reduced spray distance will produce a significantly thicker FeCoNiCrAl coating than the baseline.
The reduced spray distance will produce a strongly adherent bond coat.
The thicker coating can be obtained while maintaining minimal as-sprayed oxidation.
The resulting coating will maintain mechanical integrity during high-temperature thermal-barrier service.
The intervention remains effective for feedstock in the 15–45 μm range when the spray distance is maintained near 300–350 mm.
The intervention remains effective when coating internal diameters as small as 120 mm.

contradictions.description: A 300–350 mm nozzle-to-substrate distance is presented as applicable inside a 120 mm internal diameter, but the stated geometry does not explain how that stand-off can physically be maintained while spraying the internal surface.
